title: Natural Theorem Sequence for the 4D GSPT-SBL Framework
author: UAH.Edu (NSSTC) GSPT-SBL Research Group
abstract: The proposed natural theorem sequence provides a robust mathematical architecture for the 4D GSPT-SBL framework, effectively partitioning the complex dynamics of the stable boundary layer into verifiable analytic claims. This sequence bridges the gap between microscale turbulence and macroscale thermodynamics by identifying the Surface Energy Budget (SEB) as the generator of topological complexity.

theorems.title: Regularized Fast Critical Manifold
theorems.description: This foundational result establishes that the state space is organized around an invariant algebraic surface, $\mathcal{M}_0$, where mechanical TKE production is balanced by buoyant destruction and dissipation.

points.label: Smoothness and Existence
points.text: By implementing a $C^\infty$ hyperbolic embedding ($e_\xi^*$) and a background mixing floor ($\delta > 0$), the manifold is guaranteed to be a smooth, differentiable surface.

points.label: Forward Invariance
points.text: The framework proves that any trajectory starting in the physical domain ($e \ge -\delta$) is strictly positively invariant, preventing unphysical negative energy states.

points.label: Normal Hyperbolicity
points.text: The regularization ensures that the manifold remains normally hyperbolic and attracting away from bifurcation loci, satisfying the hypotheses of Fenichel's Theorem for manifold persistence.

theorems.title: Boundary Crossing Theorem
theorems.description: This theorem corrects legacy misconceptions by proving that turbulence extinction in the isolated atmospheric subsystem is not a "fold" but a geometric termination.

points.label: Transversal Contact
points.text: The active critical manifold $\mathcal{M}_{\text{act}}$ terminates at the physical admissibility boundary $e=0$ via transversal contact.

points.label: Non-Zero Slope
points.text: The limiting slope ($de^*/d\Delta$) as the system approaches the boundary is non-zero ($l_0^2/c_\mu$), meaning the manifold does not flatten out or turn back.

points.label: Deterministic Recovery
points.text: This "rubbery" transition allows turbulence to regrow deterministically once macro-environmental forcing ($\Delta$) crosses the regularized threshold $\Delta = \delta/l_0$.

theorems.title: Fold Illusion Theorem
theorems.description: This result formally identifies the "Fold Illusion"---the misattribution of S-shaped geometry to the isolated TKE equation.

points.label: Absence of Interior Fast Fold
points.text: Rigorous symbolic audits prove that setting the fast vector field ($\mathcal{F}$) and its derivative ($\partial_e\mathcal{F}$) to zero simultaneously yields no real, differentiable solutions in the interior ($e > 0$).

points.label: The Cusp Reality
points.text: Transformed into regularized coordinates, the isolated system reduces to a smooth cubic that yields a degenerate triple root---a cusp---strictly on the boundary.

theorems.title: Coupled Thermodynamic Fold Theorem
theorems.description: This theorem establishes that the sudden "brittle" collapse of the boundary layer is an emergent phenomenon of coupled dynamics.

points.label: SEB Coupling
points.text: A genuine S-shaped fold catastrophe ($\mathcal{C}_{\text{fold}}$) emerges only when the atmosphere is coupled to the nonlinear Surface Energy Budget (SEB).

points.label: Jacobian Rank Loss
points.text: The collapse is triggered where the slow thermodynamic map loses rank ($\partial H / \partial T_s = 0$ or $\det DF = 0$), rather than a failure of the fast TKE subsystem itself.

points.label: Thermodynamic Starvation
points.text: The collapse is recognized as a top-down, surface-driven starvation of the atmospheric subsystem, where the surface can no longer sustain a thermal equilibrium.

theorems.title: Recovery Classification
theorems.description: The final theorem categorizes nocturnal transitions into two geometrically distinct topological classes based on their governing singularities.

points.label: Rubbery Path (Boundary Re-entry)
points.text: Triggered by a transversal boundary crossing where the slow manifold remains intact. These are continuous, reversible transitions with low hysteresis and short recovery times.

points.label: Brittle Path (Catastrophic Collapse)
points.text: Triggered by crossing the coupled SEB fold ($\mathcal{C}_{\text{fold}}$). This is an irreversible, discontinuous collapse that throws the state vector off-manifold into a global phase-space excursion---the Blackadar inertial circuit---before reattachment can occur.

synthesis.intro: Organizing the manuscript around this sequence clarifies the "Fold Illusion" by separating the transversal encounter in the fast subsystem from the rank deficiency in the coupled system. This provides a unified explanation for several SBL phenomena:

points.label: Hysteresis and Intermittency
points.text: These emerge as natural topological properties of folded manifolds rather than stochastic noise or ad-hoc rules.

points.label: The RMSE Paradox
points.text: The framework explains why higher fit errors in open terrain (CASES99) are signatures of unconstrained global dynamics (inertial oscillations) rather than model failure, while high surface roughness (FLOSS) acts as a dynamic damper that pins trajectories tightly to the manifold.

points.label: Nocturnal Lifecycle
points.text: The SBL is redefined as a deterministic relaxation oscillation, where the Low-Level Jet acts as the physical "pump" that accumulates the shear necessary to force the system back to the active turbulent branch.
